You are not to give it to him now, because I don’t want him back asking me questions which I won’t answer. Now be off, you idle fellow, the wagon is nearly out of sight.’ “Jim took the note and went, and that is all I know about your brother, Sir Henry; but I am much afraid—” “Mr. Quatermain,” said Sir Henry, “I am going to look for my brother; I am going to trace him to Suliman’s Mountains, and over them if necessary, till I find him, or until I know that he is dead. Will you come with me?” I am, as I think I have said, a cautious man, indeed a timid one, and this suggestion frightened me.
